method.cold: Fresh template VM; public Maven and Gradle wrapper prewarmed; no app source, native outputs or compiler cache.
method.warm: Same VM and recipe after cold; EAS working directory recreated; Gradle, compiler and Metro caches retained.
method.endToEnd: Trigger through provisioning/setup, EAS local build, artifact upload, polling and metadata publish until APK URL ready. Warm excludes reprovisioning.
timingLimitations: One cold/warm pair per strategy, not statistically replicated.
S1 and S10 have identical cold settings but differ by 75.3 seconds: normal run variance is material.
Docker log buffering requires task-epoch envelope timing; these envelopes are not isolated compilation/configuration phases.
Core matrix completed about 34 minutes after request; Docker template/setup retries exceeded the 20-minute target.

conclusions: Raw delivered artifacts faster than Docker in both matched control runs. Docker was 13.6s faster for cold EAS only, and 11.7s slower warm.
Four workers and 6 GiB produced the lowest observed core warm time; six then eight workers produced the lowest combined end-to-end pair. Neither proves a universal default.
Compiler caching adds cold work but reduces warm compilation. Matched Docker/raw warm compiler stats: 448 direct hits, zero misses; 816 PCH-related uncacheable calls.
GC pauses were under one second on warm builds; larger heap alone is not supported as the next optimization.
Native CMake configuration remains a substantial warm cost. Parallel task durations overlap and must not be added as wall time.
No OOM recorded across the 22 completed builds.
